description.narrative: Sida stödjer UNFPAs landprogram i Sudan genom ett icke-öronmärkt programstöd på 45 miljoner SEK under perioden 2017-2020. Landprogrammets totala budget är ca 40 miljoner USD under en programperiod på fyra år. Landprogrammet implementeras inom tre strategiska områden: sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa, jämställdhet och kvinnors egenmakt samt befolkningsutveckling. Det övergripande målet för UNFPAs landprogram i Sudan är att minska mödradödlighet genom ett integrerat stöd till sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa, familjeplanering och genom att förebygga och hantera könsbaserat våld. Programmet syftar till att stärka den institutionella kapaciteten hos hälsovårdsministerier och det civila samhället inom prioriterade stater i Sudan. UNFPAs landprogram omfattar både utvecklingsinsatser och humanitärt stöd. Humanitära behov i denna kontext är ofta långvariga och kräver ett flexibelt tillvägagångssätt som stödjer både utvecklingsinsatser och humanitärt arbete.

Sida supports UNFPA's country program in Sudan through a non-earmarked programme support with SEK 45 million in period between 2017-2020. The total budget of the country programme 2018-2021 is approximately USD 40 million. The country programme is iplemented within three strategic outcome areas: sexual and reproductive health, gender equality and women's empowerment and population dynamics. The overall goal of the UNFPA country programme for Sudan is to reduce maternal deaths and disabilities through an integrated approach to sexual and eproductive health, family planning and prevention and response to gender-based violence. The programme seeks to strengthen capacities of health ministries and civil society partners at federal and priority state level. The objectives of the programme include to ensure access to high-quality sexual and reproductive services, family planning services, and preventing and responding to gender-based violence, while also increasing national capacities for data production and analysis. UNFPA's country programme includes both development and humanitarian interventions. Humanitarian needs in this context are often protracted and require a flexible approach that supports both development and humanitarian assistance.

UNFPA Suda is implementing its 7th Country Programme Cycle. The overall objective of the country programme is contributing to the Global UNFPA Strategic goal of achieving universal access to sexual and reproductive health, promoting reproductive rights, reducing maternal mortality and accelerating progress on the ICPD agenda and SDGs 3, 5 and 6 through the following outcomes. There is no financial support or capacity strengthening to the government and its institutions since the militray coup in October, 2021).
UNFPA Strategic Plan 2022-2025
Outcome 1: By 2025, the reduction in the unmet need for family planning has accelerated
Outcome 2: By 2025, the reduction of preventable maternal deaths has accelerated
Outcome 3: By 2025, the reduction in gender-based violence and harmful practices has accelerated
UN Development Assistance Framework (extended up to end of 2025):
Outcome 4: By 2021 national, state and local institutions are more effective to carry out their mandates efficiently including strengthened normative frameworks that respect human rights and fundamental freedoms and ensure effective service delivery.
Country Program Document between the Government of Sudan and UNFPA:
Output 1: Strengthened capacities of health ministries and civil society partners at federal and priority states level to ensure access to high-quality sexual and reproductive health services, including in humanitarian settings.
Output 2: Strengthened capacities of health ministries and civil society partners at federal and priority states level for better access to high-quality family planning services, including in humanitarian settings.
Output 3 Strengthened capacity of government and civil society institutions to prevent and respond to gender-based violence with a special focus on women and young girls, including in humanitarian settings
Activities for 2024 and 2025 includes:
UNFPA integrated response and thematic areas are as following: 1. Strengthening coordination for SRH response in Sudan. 2. Improved capacity of Sudan EMONC network and improve access to lifesaving SRH interventions including clinical management of rape. 3. Last Mile availability of life-saving sexual and reproductive health commodities and supplies 4. Improved capacities of skilled birth attendants including coverage specially areas with limited access. . 5. Improved coverage with essential SRH services through supporting capacity of existing PHCs and deployment of temporary clinics and on-the-wheel mobile clinics to the IDP gathering sites and affected areas with limited access to health services. 6. Community engagement and empowerment to lead and support in provision of integrated sexual and reproductive health services, including prevention and response of GBV, prevention of HIV amongst Key and vulnerable groups, the active referral of obstetric emergencies, cash and voucher assistance. 7. Improved evidence-generation to support programming and effective responses and better targeting including conducting research and studies. 8. Strengthening the mechanisms for the provision of Integrated GBV/SRH life-saving services as well as prevention and risk mitigation measures for vulnerable women and girls impacted by the conflict and subsequent displacement, famine and natural disasters. 9. Building the resilience of women, girls and the vulnerable population by supporting Livelihood Activities, provision of Dignity Kits, as well as Cash Voucher Assistance 10. Strengthening Localization and Accountability through supporting Women-led Organizations, youth and PWD organisations and initiatives 11. Addressing Social and Gender Norms to prevent GBV and harmful practices including FGM and Child Marriage. In addition to support survivors and facilitate their access to services. 12. Strengthening GBV coordination mechanism to enhance effectiveness of GBV response, strengthening resilience and preparedness, and to promote social cohesion 13. Support Youth by providing life-skills and PSS and strengthening their networks to support building the resilience of communities 14. Support PWD by providing life-skills and PSS support and strengthening PWD networks to participate in local planning, decision-making processes 15. Strengthen PSEA/ AAP to raise awareness the rights of beneficiaries and standards of conduct

description.narrative:
For a more detailed information about results reference is made to Archive 24/00028454. Statement on narrative report 2023.
Due to the difficult conditions caused by the ongoing conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces, UNFPA has been working intensively in Sudan in 2023. Contributions have focused on supporting women and girls, especially those who are pregnant or at risk of gender based violence (GBV). UNFPA, which receives flexible funding from Sida has therefore had to shift its activities from previously prioritized geographic areas to new ones in order to meet the new needs at the same time as evacuating its office and at the same reallocate its personnel to safe areas inside and outside of Sudan. One example is that after the mass displacement caused by the conflict, the focus of clinical management of rape (CMR) shifted to new states with little preexisting capacities in CMR and focus shifted to included more training on CMR and the provision of supplies.
In terms of the overall performance, the UNFPA Sudan has despite the outbreak of the civil war in April 2023, reached 65.6% of its annual planned targets in relative terms, i.e. the proportion of the actual achievements to the annual planned targets (21 out of 35 targets were achieved). The main interventions included support to service facilities (rehabilitation, renovation, equipment, furniture, supplies, commodities, and health kits) for improving access to basic services and the availability of Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (EmONC), service through health facilities, youth/women centers and mobile clinics. Other interventions were providing communities with the necessary coping mechanism and community outreach for behavior change. The gaps in midwifery coverage were worsened due to the large population movements that followed the war in April 2023.This was addressed through the deployment and redeployment of midwives to communities with a high concentration of displace people and high identified gap and providing further training for midwives.
In total, the UNFPA Sudan support reached around 857,600 direct beneficiaries with awareness, training and services (of which 460,505 people were reached with GBV response services, such as clinical management of rape, psykosocial support and materials/kits and referral to appropriate services). 7,937 service providers, including community workers and volunteers and 572 service delivery points received support .
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
